• Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution are related to the Right Against Exploitation: 
 
• Article 23
 
• Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and any act of compelling a person to work without wages.

• Article 24
 
• Prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in factories, mines, and other hazardous jobs.
 
• It also bars the employment of children between 14 and 18 years of age in any hazardous occupations. 
 
• The Right Against Exploitation is one of the fundamental rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution's Articles 12 to 35 provide for six Fundamental Rights of India.

• Articles 25–28: Deal with the freedom of religion

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding GDP is correct?

I. GDP is used to measure human development.

II. Externalities are not taken into account while estimating GDP.

III. Services provided by housewives are included while estimating GDP.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• GDP is used to measure human development.
 
 
• This statement is incorrect.
 
• GDP measures the economic output of a country but does not directly measure human development, which is better captured by indices like the Human Development Index (HDI).
 
• GDP focuses on the value of goods and services produced, not factors such as health, education, or inequality.
 
 
 
• Externalities are not taken into account while estimating GDP.
 
 
• This statement is correct.
 
• GDP does not account for externalities, which are the unintended positive or negative effects of economic activities (e.g., pollution, environmental degradation).
 
• These impacts are not reflected in GDP calculations, even though they influence societal well-being.
 
 
 
• Services provided by housewives are included while estimating GDP.
 
• This statement is incorrect.
 
 
• GDP only includes market-based activities—those involving monetary transactions.
 
• Services like household work done by housewives (or unpaid domestic labor) are not included because they do not involve monetary transactions in the formal economy.

questions.question: Conservation of biological diversity and sustainable use of its components are the main objectives of which of the following treaties/protocols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Nagoya protocol**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nagoya Protocol** is an international agreement under the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
 
• It focuses on the **conservation of biological diversity**, the **sustainable use of its components**, and the **fair and equitable sharing of benefits** arising from the utilization of genetic resources.
 
• Key Objectives:
 
• Conservation of Biological Diversity: Ensures that ecosystems, species, and genetic resources are preserved.
 
• Sustainable Use: Promotes the sustainable use of genetic resources for long-term ecological balance.
 
• Equitable Benefit Sharing: Establishes mechanisms to share the benefits derived from genetic resources with the communities or countries that provide them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rio Protocol:
 
• Refers to the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development (1992), which laid the groundwork for sustainable development principles but does not focus specifically on biodiversity.

questions.question: From which of the following countries were the principles of liberty, equality and fraternity taken in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **principles of liberty, equality, and fraternity** were taken from the French Revolution and were included in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **These ideals were integral to the democratic philosophy that influenced the Constitution, particularly in promoting individual freedoms and social justice.**
 
• These principles were central to the French motto "Liberté, égalité, fraternité", and they inspired the Indian leaders while drafting the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Kingdom:**

 
 
• India’s constitutional framework was influenced by the British model, especially the parliamentary system and the rule of law.
 
• The concept of the Cabinet system, bicameral legislature, and law-making procedure were all drawn from the UK's political system.
 
• Parliamentary sovereignty and common law were also inherited.
 
 
 
• **Ireland:**
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the Irish Constitution.
 
• Ireland’s Constitution, which emphasized social welfare and justice, influenced India's approach to socio-economic rights.
 
 
 
• **United States of America:**
 
 
• The ideas of federalism and fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the US Constitution.
 
• The system of judicial review, where courts have the power to examine and invalidate laws inconsistent with the Constitution, was another influence from the United States.

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights can be suspended during the operation of a National Emergency except the rights guaranteed by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 20 and 21**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 20 and 21** of the Indian Constitution guarantee **protection against arbitrary arrest and detention** and **the right to life and personal liberty**, respectively.
 
• These rights cannot be suspended even during the operation of a **National Emergency** (as per **Article 359** of the Constitution).
 
• Specifically, **Article 20** protects individuals against **retroactive criminal laws** and **double jeopardy**, while **Article 21** ensures that **no person can be deprived of their life or personal liberty** except according to procedure established by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 14 and 15**: These guarantee **equality before the law** and **protection against discrimination**, but they **can be suspended** during an emergency, except in certain cases of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Articles 23 and 24**: These deal with **prohibition of human trafficking** and **forced labor**, but can be suspended during an emergency.
 
• **Articles 18 and 19**: **Article 18** relates to the **abolition of titles**, and **Article 19** guarantees **freedom of speech and expression**; both can be suspended during an emergency.
